findings.where: First screen: the aqueduct drawing that fills the hero, and the small mark beside 'MMM INFRA' in the nav bar
findings.fault: The logo mark is shown in white, not in its #404040 grey and #0070C0 blue. Mark does not hold a reversed (white) version. In the hero drawing the mark is also altered: amber hatching fills the third arch and a loose S-curve trails off its right end. The direction's diazo ground cannot carry the full-colour logo, so it only works with a recoloured, redrawn mark.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo the brief says stays and is never redrawn. A first-time visitor who already knows the blue-and-grey logo from LinkedIn or a PDF would also object, because the site's mark does not match it.

findings.where: Title block / nav bar, on desktop and phone: the PROFILE, ARTICLES, BLOG and CONTACT cells next to the DRAWING MMM-GA-001 and SCALE NTS cells
findings.fault: The four links and the two static cells have the same treatment: ruled cells, tracked capitals, link-coloured text. Nothing shows which cells go somewhere. On the phone, the drawing number and scale take half of the top row, in the same style as the links.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for the way around taps 'MMM-GA-001' or 'NTS' and nothing happens. They also see a drawing number that means nothing to them in the most valuable strip of the page.

findings.where: First screen: the hatching in the third arch next to the WRITE TO MARK button
findings.fault: Sodium amber is the one action colour, and it is also used for decoration in the hero drawing in the same view. The only page action no longer owns the page's strongest colour.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor scanning for the next step, whose eye is pulled first to a hatched arch that does nothing.

findings.where: Hero name block: the circled 'A' marker and the role line 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS'
findings.fault: Mark's one-line role is set in the same style as drawing-sheet notation, so the reader gets 'Infrastructure advisor' followed straight away by section-cut jargon. The circled 'A' next to the name reads like an avatar initial or a grade. 'NTS' appears three times in the first screen.
findings.who_objects: Agency staff doing the five-second check of who this is and what he does. The second line of his role is noise to them, and it weakens the personal, plain voice the brief asks for.

findings.where: Article specimen ('The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'), on both widths
findings.fault: Long-form reading text is light text on saturated blue, with the full blueprint grid running behind every line. The page's decoration sits exactly where the reader works, on every article page.
findings.who_objects: A reader who follows a LinkedIn link to one of Mark's longer articles and has to read many paragraphs over ruled lines. Angélique would object too, because every post or PDF gateway she adds inherits that ground.

findings.where: Whole tile: the first screen and the article specimen
findings.fault: No part of the tile shows where Mark's photograph goes or how a real photograph sits on the blueprint ground. The man himself is absent from the identity, so the direction does not answer client value 3.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked to be seen. A procurement reader would also object, because a solo advisor's site needs the person's face to be trusted.

findings.fault: The direction card says the title block carries the contact, but it holds only a drawing number and a scale. Mark's email address is never shown as text anywhere. The only routes are a mailto button and a CONTACT link to '#'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a work machine where mailto opens nothing, or one who wants to copy the address into a procurement system.

findings.where: Type pair note against the article heading and name heading
findings.fault: The tile states that headings are 'ExtraBold capitals, tracked wide like a drawing title', but the article heading is set in mixed case with no tracking. The tile's own heading rule already has an exception it doesn't explain.
findings.who_objects: The layout round and Angélique, who cannot tell from the tile which heading style is the rule.

findings.where: Article specimen meta lines: '18 September 2024' in proportional type, against 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF' in mono
findings.fault: Two date formats and two faces are used for the same kind of fact on one page, and two different separators (• and ·) appear in one line. The tile's own rule puts dates in mono.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader, who sees inconsistency on a site that sells precision, and finds ISO dates less friendly than the written-out form.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the 'REPLAY THE CUT' control
findings.fault: A button is styled as an underlined text link, the treatment used for the article link in the specimen beside it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects it to take them somewhere and is surprised when it replays an animation instead.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the EASING column reading 'plot', and the note's '(#13, F5/F12)'
findings.fault: Internal ticket references and an unexplained term appear in a tile meant for Mark to judge.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who reads 'plot' and '#13, F5/F12' as jargon he can't act on.

findings.where: Texture specimen, most visibly on the phone
findings.fault: The poche panel runs flush to the box's right edge while the hatch panel is inset. An empty band with a stray dimension line sits under both, so the specimen looks cropped rather than drawn.
findings.who_objects: Mark reviewing the tile, for whom a misaligned box undercuts a direction built on draughting precision.
